subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — traffic/token distribution and burst patterns
messages:
From: Devon Park <devon@alpharise.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for AlphaRise recommendation engine

Hi Sofia,

We’re kicking off sizing discussions for a dedicated fleet to run our new recommendation/recency model. We’re expecting to move from prototype to production in Q4 and would like a quick pre-sales run to understand the fleet footprint and cost.

High level: currently ~2M monthly requests across US/NA, mostly realtime inference, some background batch scoring. We don’t yet have a clean token distribution so I’m hoping you can send a short profiling questionnaire to capture peak concurrency, prompt/response lengths, and burst behavior.

Can you loop in whoever owns capacity planning? Also include any template for usage exports (CSV) that makes it easy for us to share the data.

Thanks,
Devon Park
Head of Engineering, AlphaRise
devon@alpharise.com

--
Attachment: none (asked for template)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@alpharise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for AlphaRise recommendation engine

Hi Devon — great to hear. I’m copying Marissa and Karthik from Capacity & Pre-Sales to help run a short profiling session and translate answers into a preliminary fleet estimate.

Quick profiling questions (feel free to paste answers inline or attach a CSV):
- Expected steady-state concurrency (concurrent in-flight requests during normal business hours)
- Observed or expected peak concurrency and how long peaks last (minutes/hours/days)
- Average prompt token length and average response token length (or 10/50/90 percentile)
- Percent of calls that require streaming vs non-streaming responses
- Percent of requests that reuse KV cache / session affinity (e.g., same user/session multiple calls)
- Typical SLA targets (p50/p95/p99 latency goals) and whether hard timeouts are used
- Ratio of synchronous real-time traffic to asynchronous/batch scoring (estimate %)
- Any latency tail concerns (spikes tied to cold starts, oversized responses, etc.)
- Data retention & audit requirements for logs (days/months) — affects storage/IO footprint

If you can attach a CSV with a time-series sample (timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_id) that would be ideal. I’ll put together a short worksheet to map answers to GPU counts and SKUs.

Next steps: once we have the answers we’ll propose a canary and full-reserve plan (dedicated pool size, autoscale policy, and an ops runbook).

Best,
Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_profile_template.csv (stub) — small template for token/time-series
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@alpharise.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for AlphaRise recommendation engine

Hi Devon — quick follow from capacity perspective. Two extra data points that materially change the fleet sizing:

1) KV cache reuse: if requests within a session reuse prompt context / KV cache, that reduces per-request compute significantly. Can you indicate an estimate of requests per session and whether prompts are highly overlapping?

2) Burst cadence: do you get brief sub-minute spikes (e.g., triggered by batch promotions) or multi-hour traffic windows (e.g., marketing blasts)? The former pushes us toward lower-latency, higher-concurrency instances with more aggressive batching; the latter favors queueing + batch workers.

Also: if you have any 99th percentile token lengths (or a sample of the top 1% largest responses), please include — we model tail tokens separately. I can take a look at your CSV and sketch a few GPU + quantization options (A100/80GB, A30, or Ampere Next gen if you have region preferences).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the team through the template.

-Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Devon Park <devon@alpharise.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@alpharise.com
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for AlphaRise recommendation engine

Thanks Sofia & Karthik — below are the initial answers and I attached a small export. Let me know if you need more granularity.

Answers:
- Steady-state concurrency: ~60 concurrent in-flight requests during business hours (US PST/EST peaks)
- Observed peak concurrency: up to 240 concurrent for short bursts (~10–20 minutes) during promotions; typical peak day lasts ~2–3 hours for larger product launches
- Average prompt tokens: 120 tokens (median)
- Average response tokens: 480 tokens (median)
- 85% of calls are realtime synchronous; 15% are asynchronous batch scoring (hourly)
- Streaming: ~10% of calls use server-sent streaming for incremental results
- KV reuse: sessions typically have 3–6 requests that hit similar context (moderate cache reuse)
- SLA targets: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~150ms, p99 goal ~300ms (soft). Hard timeout: 5s
- Monthly token volume estimate: ~1.5B tokens in, ~6B tokens out
- Data retention: logs kept 90 days; audit export on request

Attachments: alpha_usage_spreadsheet.csv (time-sampled rows), sample_prompts.txt

Procurement note: I’m including procurement to start collecting cost approvals.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to do a workshop.

Devon
Head of Engineering, AlphaRise
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@alpharise.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procurement@alpharise.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: Dedicated capacity for AlphaRise recommendation engine

Devon — thanks for the detailed answers and the attachments, that’s exactly what we need. High-level summary and proposed next steps below.

Summary of key inputs: steady 60 concurrent, short bursts to 240 (10–20m), median prompt 120 / response 480 tokens, ~85% realtime, KV reuse 3–6 requests/session, p99 target ~300ms, 1.5B monthly tokens in.

Preliminary sizing (ballpark):
- Canary: 2x A100-40GB (quantized) to validate latency & cache behavior with mirrored traffic; small canary for 48–72 hours.
- Production reserved pool (initial): equivalent of ~8x A100-80GB (quantized int8) with headroom for concurrent bursts — this maps to autoscale policy: +30% burst capacity for 1 hour, and overflow routing to a warm overflow pool if bursts > 1 hour.
- Batch workers: 2–3 x A30/medium instances for async hourly scoring jobs.

Operational notes:
- We’ll model tail tokens separately for pricing and advise a streaming-enabled path for the 10% streaming calls to preserve latency.
- KV cache can reduce GPU time by ~20–30% given your 3–6 reuse estimate; we’ll validate in the canary.

Next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-min sizing workshop (Karthik + engineering) — please share 2 slots.
2) I’ll produce a short PDF (redwood_prelim_sizing.pdf) with the above assumptions and a cost estimate for your procurement team.
3) If procurement wants an initial quote we can include a 30-day reserve trial and associated SLOs.

I’ll attach the preliminary worksheet and send proposed times for the workshop.

Best,
Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
